Forum: Refugee Appeal Division (appeal tribunal).
Parties: the appellant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review (from the opening paragraphs): I dismiss this appeal for the reasons that follow.
How the layers nest here: The RAD member is the author (layer 1). The appellant and the Minister make submissions to the RAD (layer 2). The RPD decision under appeal is layer 3, and what the claimant or the Minister said to the RPD, as reported, is layer 4.

paragraphs.text: I dismiss this appeal for the reasons that follow.

XXXX XXXX is a citizen of India. He fears that he will be killed or seriously harmed by the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX if he returns to India. Mr. XXXX alleged that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in October 2015 XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. After XXXX XXXX XXXX he and his parents consulted a lawyer who drafted a letter of complaint which they sent to the highest authority XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. Mr. XXXX alleged that the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in December 2015 and June 2016, because of the letter of complaint he had sent. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX his family contacted an agent who assisted Mr. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX He made his refugee claim almost two years later in September 2018.

The Refugee Protection Division (RPD) denied Mr. XXXX claim in an oral decision on the day of the hearing. The RPD did not find credible Mr. XXXX account of the events that led him to leave India and to claim refugee status in Canada. The RPD found Mr. XXXX evidence was not credible because of contradictory testimony about his efforts to find witnesses after he was advised to do so by his Indian lawyer, his omission from his written narrative that his village sarpanch and council assisted to get him XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and contradictory testimony about the timing of the steps he took to leave India. Mr. XXXX challenges these findings.

My role is to look at all the evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.1 The RPD was correct to find that Mr. XXXX is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection. I agree with Counsel that the RPD erred in relation to one of the reasons it gave for finding Mr. XXXX not credible. However, despite this error, the RPD was correct to find that Mr. XXXX account of the events that led him to leave India and the risk he would face if he returned to India were not credible. ANALYSIS Contradictory testimony about search for witnesses for claim against police

Mr. XXXX Counsel argued that the RPD erred in finding that Mr. XXXX inability to consistently testify about his efforts to make a complaint XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX including finding witnesses, undermined the credibility of his allegations. She argued that the RPD did not take into account that the events relating to his claim went back to 2015 and therefore he might not have remembered everything that the lawyer he consulted in India told him about seeking witnesses in order to pursue XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. She argued that the RPD's finding on this issue was an example of the member searching in the evidence to find something to undermine Mr. XXXX credibility. I do not agree with these arguments for the following reasons.

A key issue in this case was Mr. XXXX allegation that the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Mr. XXXX testified that, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX he consulted a lawyer who drafted a detailed complaint which he sent to the highest authority XXXX XXXX XXXX. When the RPD asked Mr. XXXX whether the lawyer had given him any other advice other than simply drafting a letter for him, Mr. XXXX said no.2 When the RPD asked him whether the lawyer had told him anything else, he said no, nothing else.

At this point, the RPD noted that in the letter that Mr. XXXX submitted from the lawyer, it said that the lawyer had advised Mr. XXXX to attempt to find witnesses in order to pursue XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. The letter from the lawyer also indicated that Mr. XXXX father had told the lawyer that attempts were made to get witnesses but no one was willing to appear. The RPD asked Mr. XXXX whether he or anyone in his family tried to get witnesses to assist with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX He replied that his family may have tried but he did not know anything about it.3 The RPD later asked him whether he had tried to find witnesses and he said no that he did not leave the house much.4 When the RPD asked why he did not try to find witnesses, he said that no one would want to get involved in the case. The RPD then asked him how he would know that if he did not ask anyone and, at this point, Mr. XXXX altered his evidence to say that he had asked a friend to be a witness but he did not want to get involved.5 When the RPD asked him why just a minute before he said that he had not looked for any witnesses, Mr. XXXX said that his family members did it and he only spoke to the one friend and no one else.6

In my view, Mr. XXXX provided contradictory testimony on several points for which he failed to provide a reasonable explanation at the hearing. While Counsel now seeks to argue that he maybe did not remember everything that his counsel told him several years earlier, Mr. XXXX did not provide this explanation when asked about his failure to mention the advice he had received and his search for witnesses. Instead, he gave evolving testimony, first saying that his family may have searched for witnesses but he knew nothing about it and that he himself had not search for witnesses because no one would want to get involved. He then altered this testimony to say that he asked a friend but he did not want to get involved. He also testified that his family had searched for witnesses but he just asked the one friend which contradicted his previous testimony that his family may have searched for witnesses but he knew nothing about it.

For the above reasons, I find that the RPD was correct to have concerns about Mr. XXXX contradictory and evolving testimony about the complaint he allegedly made XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX I note further that it is concerning that Mr. XXXX did not seek to obtain a copy of the letter of complaint that his lawyer in India had sent XXXX XXXX XXXX. While Mr. XXXX did obtain a letter from the lawyer, the lawyer did not include a copy of the letter that he had sent to XXXX XXXX XXXX on Mr. XXXX behalf. Omission of involvement of village sarpanch and council

Mr. XXXX Counsel argues that the RPD erred in finding that Mr. XXXX credibility was negatively affected by his omission from his written narrative that his village sarpanch and council assisted him to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Counsel argued that the RPD failed to take into account the explanation offered by Mr.

I do not agree with these arguments. As with the issue of the steps Mr. XXXX took as part of his complaint XXXX XXXX XXXX, discussed above, Mr. XXXX gave inconsistent testimony about the involvement of the village sarpanch and council. When the RPD asked Mr. XXXX how it was that he came to be XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Mr. XXXX replied that his family XXXX XXXX XXXX that he had not done anything wrong and that his family XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX7 When the RPD asked Mr. XXXX how the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX he said he did not know and that his family would know. It was only when the RPD asked him about the village sarpanch that Mr. XXXX said that the village sarpanch also had been involved XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX When the RPD asked him why, in his written narrative, he had not mentioned the involvement of the village sarpanch and council, Mr. XXXX replied that it was because his family had to literally beg the village sarpanch to get involved.8 When the RPD asked Mr. XXXX how many times the sarpanch went to help his parents, he said that his family would know that. The RPD then asked how he knew that the sarpanch was involved at all and he said that his family told him that reputed members of the village were involved. When the RPD asked Mr. XXXX who else was involved in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX he said that he did not know and that his family would know. Mr. XXXX gave this type of answer several times about his family knowing key information relating to his claim. I note that he did not call any family members to testify at the hearing nor did he file any affidavits or statements from family members to support his claim.

I do not agree with counsel that the RPD failed to take into account Mr. XXXX explanation for his omission of any mention of the sarpanch and council in his written narrative and, I would add, his initial testimony in response to the RPD's questions. The RPD did take into account Mr. XXXX explanations but it did not find them satisfactory to explain the omission. Mr. XXXX explanation was that his family had to beg the sarpanch to get involved. I agree with the RPD that this does not satisfactorily explain Mr. XXXX omission of the sarpanch's involvement. I also do not agree with Counsel that it is a relevant or satisfactory explanation to say that the affidavits that Mr. XXXX submitted from the sarpanch and his friend mentioned that they worked with Mr. XXXX family to XXXX XXXX XXXX. The issue was that, despite attaching these letters to his claim, Mr. XXXX made no mention of the involvement of the village sarpanch and council either in his written narrative or in his response to the RPD's questions about how he came to be XXXX XXXX XXXX.

I do not find that Mr. XXXX failure to mention the involvement of the village sarpanch and council XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is a mere peripheral detail. Mr. XXXX submitted an affidavit from the sarpanch in support of his claim. In this context, it is significant that he completely omitted any mention of the involvement of the sarpanch until prompted by the RPD.

For the above reasons, I do not find that the RPD erred in finding that Mr. XXXX failure to mention the involvement of the village sarpanch and council negatively affected his account of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Contradictory testimony about timing of steps leading to departure

Mr. XXXX Counsel argued that the RPD erred in finding that Mr. XXXX credibility was negatively affected by contradictory testimony he gave regarding the timing of his decision to leave India. Mr. XXXX Counsel argues that the RPD failed to take into account Mr. XXXX testimony that he started thinking about leaving India XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

I agree with Counsel that Mr. XXXX testimony was not necessarily contradictory as to the timing of his plans to leave India. The fact that he took an English exam in December 2015 but XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX does not undermine the credibility of his account of events. The fact that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX also does not bolster the credibility of his account XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. It is simply a neutral factor. Delay in claiming refugee status

While the RPD did not rely on Mr. XXXX two-year delay in claiming refugee status in its decision, the issue was fully canvassed at the hearing. In my view, this delay has a significant adverse effect on the credibility of Mr. XXXX allegations as to the risk he would face if he returned to India.

Mr. XXXX arrived in Canada in XXXX XXXX and he did not claim refugee protection until October 2018. When the RPD asked Mr. XXXX why he did not claim refugee status sooner, he said that he did not know anything about claiming in refugee status and he said he had not asked the agent who secured XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX about it. He also said he was staying with friends but had no relatives in Canada who could provide him with advice. He said he finally claimed refugee status when his "uncle" (friend of his brother-in-law) suggested it. In her submissions at the hearing, Mr. XXXX Counsel argued that Mr. XXXX delay in claiming refugee status should not affect his credibility because he had a student visa at the time and therefore he had a legal status in Canada.

I disagree with this argument. While it is true that Mr. XXXX had a student visa, he was not in fact studying as required for that visa. Mr. XXXX testified that he only XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and he was scared that the same things would happen to him in Canada as in India. He testified that his sister is now in Canada also so he worried about his parents being back in India alone. Regardless of the reasons that Mr. XXXX was not studying, the key issue is that he was not actually pursuing studies in Canada and therefore his student visa - that is, his status in Canada -- was not secure. In these circumstances, I find that Mr. XXXX delay in claiming refugee status is relevant and adversely affects the credibility of his account of the risk he would face if he returned to India. I also do not find the reasons he gave for his delay satisfactory. I do not find it credible that, as a college educated young person, Mr. XXXX would not have the ability to search the internet to learn about the options available to him to stay in Canada. As for the fact that he did not have relatives in Canada, Mr. XXXX testified that he was staying with friends. Therefore, he had friends from whom he could seek assistance and he also had the "uncle" who eventually advised him in relation to claiming refugee protection.

For all these reasons, I find that Mr. XXXX two-year delay in applying for refugee protection adversely affects the credibility of his account of the risk he would face in returning to India. The issue of delay is not determinative of the claim. However, it is a factor to consider along with the rest of the evidence in this case. Overall credibility assessment

In my view, the credibility concerns on which the RPD was correct, added to Mr. XXXX significant delay in claiming refugee status, are sufficient to rebut the presumption of truthfulness in this case and to find that Mr. XXXX has failed to credibly establish his allegations on a balance of probabilities. In my view, the documentary evidence submitted by Mr. XXXX is insufficient to overcome the credibility concerns arising from his testimony and delay in seeking refugee status. As noted above, Mr. XXXX gave testimony that was inconsistent with the contents of the letter from his lawyer in India as well as the affidavits from the village sarpanch and his friend in India. Mr. XXXX did submit XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX or the events that led to them.

For the above reasons, I dismiss the appeal and confirm the decision of the RPD that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
